title: What Is Information, Really?
question: Is information a physical quantity, a mathematical abstraction, or something that only exists relative to a mind?
summary: Shannon made information measurable by ignoring meaning. Physics, computation and biology each bend the concept further, hinting that information may be as fundamental as energy.
content:
A word everyone uses and nobody pinned down

We speak of information as if it were a substance: it flows, it is stored, it is lost. Yet until 1948 nobody had a precise definition. Then Claude Shannon, working on telephone communication, supplied one so useful that it underlies every digital device you own.

Shannon: information as surprise

Shannon defined information not by meaning but by uncertainty removed. A message that tells you something you already knew carries no information. A fair coin flip carries one bit, the answer to one yes/no question. The measure, entropy, is highest when outcomes are most unpredictable. Crucially, he proved that any noisy channel has a maximum rate at which data can be sent with arbitrarily few errors, which is why your phone can be accurate over a crackling radio link.

The deliberate omission of meaning

Shannon was explicit that semantic aspects of messages are irrelevant to the engineering problem. A random string and a Shakespeare sonnet of equal length can have similar Shannon entropy. This is a strength for engineering and a limitation for philosophy: his theory says how much is transmitted, not what it is about.

Kolmogorov: information as description length

Algorithmic information theory offers a different angle. The information in an object is the length of the shortest program that produces it. A million repetitions of "01" is simple, because a short program prints it. A truly random string cannot be compressed. This makes randomness and complexity precise, and it is uncomputable in general, a close cousin of the halting problem.

Information meets physics

Landauer showed that erasing a bit has a minimum thermodynamic cost, tying information to heat and entropy and resolving Maxwell's demon. Black hole thermodynamics suggests the maximum information in a region scales with its surface area, not its volume, which inspired the holographic principle. John Wheeler's "it from bit" proposes that physical things derive their existence from yes/no answers, a bold claim that remains speculative.

Where it leaves us

Information appears to be neither purely physical nor purely mental. It is a relation: a pattern that makes a difference to some receiver. Biology adds another layer, since DNA, hormones and neurons all act as channels, and what counts as signal depends on the organism interpreting it.

perspectives.title: Communication engineering
perspectives.description: Shannon entropy quantifies uncertainty resolved, giving hard limits on compression and noisy-channel capacity without reference to meaning.

perspectives.title: Computer science
perspectives.description: Kolmogorov complexity defines information as shortest description. It captures randomness precisely but cannot be computed in general.

perspectives.title: Physics
perspectives.description: Landauer's principle ties erasure to heat, and black hole entropy suggests spacetime itself may encode information on boundaries.

perspectives.title: Philosophy of mind and biology
perspectives.description: Meaning may require an interpreter. A pattern is information only for a system that can act on the difference it makes.

openQuestions: Is information fundamental to physics, or just a useful bookkeeping tool?
Can meaning ever be reduced to a quantity like entropy?
Does the black hole information paradox show information is conserved at the deepest level?
What would a theory unifying syntactic and semantic information look like?
